digest.component_or_area: rebar review CLI verb and library surface retirement
propositions: rebar review is a single-pass LLM ticket review operation that is superseded from above by the signed review-plan gate and from below by deterministic check operations, and must be safely retired without breaking external importers or scripted callers.

The CLI verb rebar review must become a deprecation shim that forwards to review-plan with --no-sign=true to preserve the old read-only semantics, rejects --graph and positional reviewer_id with exit 2, and emits a loud deprecation signal on stderr.

The library entry point rebar.llm.review_ticket and MCP tool review_ticket must be split into a private _review_ticket_impl(…) and a public facade that emits a DeprecationWarning, so that three internal harnesses (review_workflows.diff_review_paths, eval_solver, and the MCP tool itself) can call the private impl without double-signalling.

Three deprecation rows must be registered in src/rebar/_deprecations.py for cli:rebar review, lib:rebar.llm.review_ticket, and mcp:review_ticket, all marked scheduled (not permanent) with remove_in=v1.0.0, and three derived-file outputs (index.json from front-matter, docs/cli-reference.md from gen_cli_reference.py, docs/mcp-reference.md from tool docstrings) must be regenerated to point callers at review-plan.

The OUTPUT_SCHEMAS mapping must be repointed so OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["review"] resolves to PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT (the shim's output), and a synthetic "review_ticket" key must wire to REVIEW_RESULT (the legacy library/MCP output), so that no schema is orphaned and the shim's JSON is never described as an unsigned review_result.

A behavioural divergence must be accepted and documented: the old verb would run the LLM on any ticket and return findings, while the new shim fast-fails with exit 2 and no LLM call on non-claimable tickets (closed/idea/blocked), and existing tests must be updated to expect this new fast-fail contract while fourteen unedited direct callers of the public library op must remain green to prove behaviour-preservation.
